name: Omaha
description: Omaha is a community-card poker variant where each player receives four hole cards and must use exactly two of them with exactly three of the five board cards to make their best five-card hand. The constraint makes hand-reading and drawing significantly different from Texas Hold'em.

content.text: Omaha is a community-card poker variant where each player receives four hole cards and must use exactly two of them with exactly three of the five board cards to make their best five-card hand. The constraint makes hand-reading and drawing significantly different from Texas Hold'em.

Omaha emerged in the 1980s, likely in casino card rooms, and rapidly became a staple of both live and online poker. It derives from Texas Hold'em but adds the mandatory two-from-hand, three-from-board rule.
Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.
Each player receives four hole cards face-down. Five community cards are dealt in stages: flop (3), turn (1), river (1).

items.text: Omaha High: Standard pot-limit or fixed-limit; only the best high hand wins.
Omaha Hi-Low 8-or-Better: Pot splits between best high and best qualifying low (8-high or better). Commonly fixed-limit.
Five Card Omaha (Big O): Each player receives five hole cards; must still use exactly two with three board cards.
Six Card Omaha: Six hole cards; must use exactly two with three board cards.
Courchevel: One board card is dealt face-up before the first betting round; popular in France.
